categories.name: Impersonation Scams
categories.description: Scammers disguise themselves as trusted individuals, authority figures, or organizations to deceive victims into transferring funds.

subtypes.name: Friend / Family Emergency Impersonation
subtypes.description: Attacker claims to be a relative or friend experiencing an urgent crisis (hospital emergency, police detention, stranded travel).

subtypes.name: Employee / Boss Impersonation (CEO Fraud)
subtypes.description: Attacker impersonates a company manager or business owner requesting an immediate payment to a vendor or client.

subtypes.name: Bank / Telecom Official Impersonation
subtypes.description: Attacker poses as a representative from CBE, Telebirr, or Ethio Telecom claiming account blocking, system maintenance, or security updates.

subtypes.name: Organization / NGO Impersonation
subtypes.description: Attacker claims to represent a charitable foundation, government office, or church requesting donations or registration fees.

categories.name: Fake Seller & E-commerce Fraud
categories.description: Attacker advertises goods or services online, requests upfront mobile payment, and vanishes without delivering the item.

subtypes.name: Advance Payment for Electronics/Vehicles
subtypes.description: Promising discounted mobile phones, electronics, or motor vehicles upon partial or full deposit.

subtypes.name: Fake Instagram / Telegram Clothing Store
subtypes.description: Fake boutique pages collecting payments for clothes or shoes without physical inventory or shop location.

categories.name: Investment & Ponzi Schemes
categories.description: Fraudulent financial schemes promising unrealistic guaranteed returns, daily interest, or referral bonuses.

subtypes.name: Pyramid / Ponzi Multi-Level Scam
subtypes.description: Victims are persuaded to deposit funds into a pooled account with promises of passive daily income and recruitment rewards.

subtypes.name: Online Task / Freelance Deposit Scam
subtypes.description: Victims are hired for easy online tasks (liking YouTube videos, reviewing products) but must deposit funds to unlock earnings.

categories.name: Urgent & Pressure Scams
categories.description: Exploiting high-emotion situations to force rapid fund transfers before the victim can verify facts.

subtypes.name: Fake Accidental Transfer Refund
subtypes.description: Attacker sends a fake SMS mimicking a mobile money credit notification, then calls asking for a refund of the 'accidentally sent' funds.

subtypes.name: Hospital / Police Emergency Hoax
subtypes.description: Attacker calls pretending to be a doctor or police officer demanding immediate payment for a relative's treatment or bail.

categories.name: Fake Prize & Lottery Scams
categories.description: Victim is informed they won a large prize or promotion but must pay tax, processing fees, or airtime first.

subtypes.name: Telecom / Car Giveaway Fee
subtypes.description: Fake notification claiming the victim won a vehicle or millions in ETB, requiring a delivery or fee payment.

categories.name: Account Takeover & OTP Harvesting
categories.description: Attempts to gain unauthorized access to victim mobile banking accounts or social media accounts.

subtypes.name: SMS OTP / PIN Phishing
subtypes.description: Attacker triggers a password reset on victim's account and tricks the victim into sharing the 4-6 digit SMS confirmation code.
